For **PostgreSQL**, ``delete retain`` and ``delete before`` order backups using the timeline and WAL segment embedded in each backup name by default. Pass the global flag ``--use-sentinel-time`` on ``delete`` to order by backup start time from sentinel/metadata when it is available; see PostgreSQL.md.

Cratis Chronicle is an open-source (MIT) event-sourcing database and runtime for applications that need a history of meaningful changes. Record application changes as events, build queryable views with declarative projections, and react to events from .NET, TypeScript, Kotlin/Java, or Elixir.

Chronicle's declarative projections map events onto **read models**, views shaped for the queries your application serves. The kernel handles processing and storage updates. **Reactors** run your code when events arrive, for example to send a notification. Materialized views update after the append, so choose the consistency behavior your workflow needs.

For personal data, Chronicle encrypts fields marked as **personally identifiable information (PII)** under a subject's key and supports erasing that key without removing the event's position in the log. These mechanisms support your compliance work; they do not make an application compliant by themselves. Read Compliance before recording personal data.

The Orleans-based .NET kernel has a first-class .NET SDK and additional TypeScript, Kotlin/Java (JVM), and Elixir clients; a Python client is coming soon. Storage providers include MongoDB (default), PostgreSQL, SQL Server, SQLite, and in-memory implementations. Client and provider capabilities differ, so use the guide for your chosen setup. Chronicle and its bundled web workbench run without Studio, Arc, or Components. Chronicle is free to use and MIT licensed; free AI skills are also available for working with the code and documentation.
- ⚙️ **Chronicle Kernel** — the server that manages event storage, processing, and querying, built on Microsoft Orleans for distributed, stateful processing
- 🌍 **Language-agnostic gRPC contracts** — protobuf contracts that any language can implement, with clients for TypeScript, Kotlin/Java, and Elixir, and a Python client coming soon
- ⌨️ **CLI** — the Cratis CLI brings event, observer, projection, and read-model inspection to the terminal

On the panel, one Go interface: a JSON Schema for its settings (the admin builds the form from it), validation, the spec a node runs, credential issuing, and its piece of each subscription format.
